title: GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis: expose the Wave screen's 5-day lookback result (wave_showed_pullback/wave_showed_rally), not just today's state
description:
Filed from frontend-signal-why-explanation's own checklist item 1 (a genuine data-availability gap discovered while implementing the stock-detail 'why this signal' explanation balloon): `_determine_signal` (backend/app/signals/engine.py) doesn't gate BUY/SELL on today's `evaluate_wave` result alone -- it gates on `wave_showed_pullback`/`wave_showed_rally` (`_wave_lookback`), true if the qualifying OVERSOLD_PULLBACK/OVERBOUGHT_RALLY state appeared on *any* of the last `_WAVE_LOOKBACK_DAYS` (5) trading days, not just today. `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/analysis`'s `screens.wave.state` only ever reports *today's* `evaluate_wave` result, so a client consuming this endpoint has no way to distinguish 'the Wave condition was met on an earlier day within the lookback window' from 'the Wave condition was never met at all' -- both currently just look like `screens.wave.state != OVERSOLD_PULLBACK/OVERBOUGHT_RALLY` today.

This is invisible for a fresh BUY/SELL itself (the signal's own existence already proves the lookback condition held at some point), but matters for anything trying to *explain* the signal causally: frontend-signal-why-explanation's HOLD explanation can only conclusively rule out the Wave condition today when Tide/Impulse/Trigger all otherwise line up for a directional trade (by elimination -- see that task's `signalExplanation.ts`); every other HOLD configuration has to render an honest 'can't be confirmed from today's data alone' caveat rather than a definitive met/not-met, purely because this field isn't exposed. Extending the API to expose `wave_showed_pullback`/`wave_showed_rally` (or an equivalent, e.g. `wave.showed_pullback_in_lookback: bool`) would let that caveat be replaced with a fully accurate statement in every case, closing the gap `_wave_lookback`'s own docstring already names explicitly.

Add the exposure as a new field (or two) on `WaveScreen` in `backend/app/api/schemas.py`, sourced from `_wave_lookback`'s existing return values (already computed internally by `analyse()` -- no new computation needed, just plumbing the two booleans that are currently discarded after `_determine_signal` consumes them). Update `backend/openapi.json` and regenerate `frontend/src/api/types.ts` per the add-api-endpoint skill's contract-sync step. A frontend follow-up to actually consume the new field(s) in `signalExplanation.ts` (removing the `met: null` ambiguous-case branch) is out of this task's own scope -- file that separately once this lands, or fold it in here if it's cheap enough once the schema change is done; record whichever choice as a decisions entry.

checklist.step: Decide the exact field shape (e.g. WaveScreen.showed_pullback_in_lookback: bool | null, WaveScreen.showed_rally_in_lookback: bool | null, null when Tide is Neutral since neither is ever reachable) and document it with a description citing docs/Analyse.md §5 and _wave_lookback's own docstring; record as a decisions entry.
Plumb _wave_lookback's existing wave_showed_pullback/wave_showed_rally return values through analyse() into the screens.wave dict instead of discarding them after _determine_signal consumes them.
Update backend/app/api/schemas.py's WaveScreen model, regenerate backend/openapi.json, and regenerate frontend/src/api/types.ts.
Unit tests covering: a directional tide where the lookback state differs from today's state (the case this field exists to distinguish), and the Tide-Neutral case.

Decide and record (as a decisions entry) whether to fold in the frontend-signal-why-explanation follow-up (consuming the new field(s) to remove signalExplanation.ts's ambiguous-caveat branch) here or file it as its own separate task.

decisions.decision: WaveScreen gains two new required (non-optional in the OpenAPI schema) fields, `showed_pullback_in_lookback: bool | None` and `showed_rally_in_lookback: bool | None`, plumbed straight from `_wave_lookback`'s existing `(wave_showed_pullback, wave_showed_rally)` return values. Both are `None` only when `screens.tide.trend == "NEUTRAL"`; for a directional tide, both are real (non-null) booleans -- including the direction that's structurally always `False` for that tide (e.g. `showed_rally_in_lookback` when tide is BULLISH), since `_wave_lookback` itself already returns `False` (not some third state) for the unreachable direction, and that `False` is a real fact about the current tide, not a placeholder.
decisions.rationale: This is exactly the shape the task's own checklist item 1 proposed, and it matches _wave_lookback's own existing internal representation with the minimum possible transformation (only overriding to None for the one case -- Neutral tide -- where _wave_lookback's own False,False return would misleadingly read as 'checked, and it didn't happen' rather than 'not applicable, no direction to check against'). Alternative considered and rejected: a single tri-state field (e.g. `wave_lookback_state: 'PULLBACK' | 'RALLY' | 'NONE' | null`) collapsing both booleans into one -- rejected because it doesn't mirror _wave_lookback's own two-boolean contract as directly, forces the client to re-derive which boolean matters for a given tide instead of the API doing it, and the two-field shape was already explicitly proposed in this task's own checklist. Also rejected: making both fields None whenever they're not the 'reachable' direction for the current tide (i.e. None instead of False for the always-unreachable one even on a directional tide) -- rejected because the checklist explicitly scoped the null case to 'when Tide is Neutral', and because _wave_lookback's own docstring already treats the unreachable-direction False as a real, deliberate return value (see its 'only one of the two showed booleans is ever reachable per call; the other is set to False directly' passage), not an undefined one -- overriding it to null here would be inventing a distinction the domain layer itself doesn't draw.
decisions.alternatives_considered: single tri-state field; None for the always-False unreachable direction on a directional tide

decisions.decision: The frontend-signal-why-explanation follow-up (consuming the new field(s) in signalExplanation.ts to remove its ambiguous-caveat branch) is filed as its own separate task, docs/tasks/frontend-signal-wave-lookback-explanation.json (skill: add-frontend-feature, depends_on: [api-stocks-analysis-wave-lookback]), rather than folded into this task.
decisions.rationale: Consuming the field is a real rewrite of a dense branching chain in explainSignal (the waveMetToday / signal!=='HOLD' / impulseMet&&triggerMet / else chain) plus a fixture/test rewrite across signalExplanation.test.ts and SignalExplanationContent.test.tsx's ambiguousWaveScreens, and a docstring update describing the now-resolved gap -- meaningfully more than 'cheap enough to fold in' once the schema change landed. It's also governed by a different skill (add-frontend-feature, with its own common/-vs-feature-specific placement and Storybook/test-coverage bar) than this task's add-api-endpoint, matching the api-watchlist/api-stocks-indicator-history precedent this task's own description already cited for keeping a schema change and its frontend consumer as separate tasks. Regenerating frontend/src/api/types.ts and fixing every now-broken WaveScreen/Screens object literal across the frontend test suite (a required, non-optional schema field breaking every existing literal that didn't include it) was still done in this task, since that's the add-api-endpoint skill's own required contract-sync step, not the deeper consumer-logic rewrite being deferred.
decisions.alternatives_considered: folding the full signalExplanation.ts rewrite into this task
